name: Viatika
tagline: Unlock the Power of the x402 Web. Without the Chaos.
description: Viatika is an enterprise accounting and payment abstraction layer for x402-powered services. It functions as a 'Brex for blockchain' — enterprises buy credits from Viatika, provision employees with spending policies, and Viatika's SDK intercepts x402 Payment Required responses and settles them using its own HSM-backed wallet. The company is incorporated as Skapa OÜ dba Viatika.

designNotes.colorPalette: Dark navy/deep blue primary background with white text and a blue-accent CTA button; clean two-tone contrast palette
designNotes.typography: Albert Sans (headings), system sans-serif body — clean and corporate with modern spacing
designNotes.layout: Long-form scroll marketing page; problem/solution narrative structure with full-width sections; left-aligned text blocks with large typographic headers
designNotes.heroSection: Bold headline 'Unlock the Power of the x402 Web. Without the Chaos.' with a 'Join the Waitlist' CTA and minimalist above-the-fold layout
ctas: Join the Waitlist (links to Google Form)

userFlow: Enterprise signs up to waitlist → buys credits → Viatika provisions employee accounts with spending limits → employees use any x402-enabled service transparently → finance team gets reconciliation exports for QuickBooks/Xero/SAP
valueProposition: Enterprises want to access x402-powered AI tools and services but face two blockers: (1) giving employees crypto wallets is a security/training nightmare, and (2) thousands of microtransactions are impossible to reconcile in traditional accounting systems. Viatika eliminates both problems by acting as the crypto layer on behalf of the enterprise.
businessModel: Credit-based SaaS — enterprises pre-purchase credits from Viatika (likely with markup). Revenue comes from spread on x402 transaction volume plus potential SaaS fees for policy management and accounting integrations.
strengths: Extremely clear problem/solution narrative targeting a real friction point in enterprise x402 adoption
Finance team reconciliation angle is a non-obvious but powerful wedge — differentiated from consumer wallets
HSM-backed centralized settlement reduces enterprise security concerns
Integrations with QuickBooks, Xero, SAP address CFO buying criteria directly
Landing page is polished and conversion-focused (waitlist CTA with Google Form)
weaknesses: Currently waitlist-only — no live product, no public demo or pricing
Centralized custodial model contradicts crypto ethos, may deter blockchain-native buyers
Very early stage — OG metadata still points to localhost:3000 (staging artifact in production)
No visible team page, investor backing, or social proof
Relies entirely on x402 adoption momentum — if x402 stagnates, so does Viatika
lessonsForPCC: Viatika's 'abstraction layer' framing is directly applicable to PCC: enterprises adopting on-chain capability verification face identical friction (wallets, gas, reconciliation). PCC could position its operator dashboard as the enterprise abstraction layer for physical capability services — hiding USDC/escrow complexity behind familiar job management UX. The 'finance team needs clean exports' insight is powerful — PCC should offer QuickBooks/CSV export of operator payment history alongside its crypto rails.
